title: No HTTP auth on any route in standalone/make-up/Docker boot; startup token gates only GET /readyz and only under desktop-child
repro: ARXMCP_BOOTSTRAP_MODE=1 ARXMCP_BIND_PORT=7803 uv run python -m server.main ; then: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7803/debug/cache-stats ; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7803/ui/api/notebooks ; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7803/metrics/ ; all return 200 with no X-ArXMCP-Startup-Token header.
observed: All routes (/debug/cache-stats, /ui/api/notebooks incl. POST/PATCH/DELETE mutation routes, /metrics, /mcp, /status) answer without any auth. The X-ArXMCP-Startup-Token is enforced ONLY by ReadyzStartupTokenMiddleware, which (per its own docstring) is 'constructed EXCLUSIVELY by this module's boot path ... never registered inside server.main.create_app' and gates ONLY path == /readyz. So `python -m server.main`, `make up`, and docker/Dockerfile.server run with zero request auth on every route.
expected: Documented loopback-only posture (Threat 4) treats localhost as the trust boundary, so no per-route auth is by design. Flagged because the mutation-capable /ui/api/notebooks surface and /debug are fully unauthenticated to any local process; the only auth control in the codebase (startup token) covers a single read endpoint in a single boot mode.
code_ref: server/desktop_child.py:121 (ReadyzStartupTokenMiddleware); server/main.py:842-900 (route mounts, no auth dependency)

title: GET /ui/api/notebooks leaks absolute filesystem paths unauthenticated (home dir, source tree, stale pytest tmp path)
observed: Response lists every notebook with absolute lancedb_path values, e.g. "/Users/chris.dare/Personal/SourceCode/arXMCP/var/arxmcp/notebooks/browser-pass-check/lancedb" and a STALE test entry "my-notebook" pointing at "/private/tmp/claude-501/pytest-of-chris.dare/pytest-49/test_init_happy_path0/notebooks/my-notebook/lancedb" (a pytest tmp dir that no longer exists). No auth required.
expected: A desktop UI list endpoint need not expose absolute host paths; returning slug + display metadata would avoid disclosing the user's home dir and source-tree layout to any local process / browser (webview) request. The dead pytest-tmp notebook also indicates a test run leaked a row into the production notebooks store.

title: /metrics/ ASGI app answers 200 to every HTTP verb incl TRACE/DELETE/PATCH/PUT/HEAD/OPTIONS
repro: for m in OPTIONS TRACE PATCH HEAD DELETE PUT; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$m %{http_code}\n" -X $m http://127.0.0.1:7803/metrics/; done
observed: All six verbs return 200 with the Prometheus body (every other route correctly returns 405). TRACE and PATCH/DELETE on /metrics are answered as if GET.
expected: prometheus_client's make_asgi_app does not method-gate; a metrics endpoint should accept GET/HEAD only. TRACE in particular should be 405. Low risk (no reflection, loopback) but inconsistent with the 405 discipline on all other routes.

title: No inbound URL-length or header-size cap: 60 KB URL and 90 KB header value both accepted
observed: 60 KB URL -> 405 (routed, not rejected as 414); 90 KB single header value -> 200. The 1 MB body cap (RequestBodySizeLimitMiddleware) does not cover the request line or headers.
expected: A 1 MB body cap exists but there is no equivalent bound on URL length (expect 414) or header size (expect 431). On loopback the memory-pressure risk is minor, but a malicious local process can force large per-request allocations that bypass the documented body cap.

title: MCP validation/error responses leak internal pydantic + handler class names
repro: python3 scratchpad/api/handshake.py  # batch-array case ; and scratchpad/api/fuzz.py  # any bad-arg case
observed: JSON-RPC batch array -> 400 'Validation error: 4 validation errors for JSONRPCMessage\nJSONRPCRequest\n  Input should be a valid dictionary...'. Bad tool args -> 'Error executing tool search_papers: 1 validation error for handle_search_papersArguments'. Internal class names (JSONRPCMessage, JSONRPCRequest, handle_<tool>Arguments) surface to the client.
expected: Error bodies to an untrusted MCP client should not echo internal class/function names; they reveal the handler naming convention and pydantic model structure. Library-level (mcp / FastMCP) but still exposed. Low.
code_ref: server/tools.py (FastMCP tool wrappers); mcp streamable_http layer

title: MCP initialize accepts garbage/wrong-type protocolVersion (int 12345, '9999-99-99') with HTTP 200
repro: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7803/mcp/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":12345,"capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"x","version":"0"}}}'
observed: protocolVersion=12345 (int) and protocolVersion='9999-99-99' both return 200 and negotiate protocolVersion '2025-11-25'. No type check or rejection of the malformed/unsupported value.
expected: A non-string protocolVersion should be a 400/invalid-params. Downgrading an unknown STRING version to the server's latest is spec-acceptable, but silently accepting a non-string type is lax input handling at the MCP boundary. Low.

title: session.py docstring claims omitting Mcp-Session-Id skips cap enforcement ('known bypass'); MCP layer 400s first, making the comment stale/misleading
observed: tools/call with no Mcp-Session-Id -> HTTP 400 {'code':-32600,'message':'Bad Request: Missing session ID'} from the MCP StreamableHTTP session manager, BEFORE SessionCapMiddleware can 'skip enforcement'. The documented bypass (a) is unreachable via the /mcp endpoint.
expected: server/session.py module docstring lists '(a) omitting Mcp-Session-Id skips cap enforcement outright' as a known, admitted bypass. Empirically it cannot be exercised (MCP rejects first). A security-relevant comment that overstates an attack path is misleading for future maintainers; either the comment or the middleware ordering should be corrected.

title: Startup config errors dump full Python traceback; 0.0.0.0 rejection leaks entire Config dict incl. data_dir path
repro: ARXMCP_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 ARXMCP_BIND_PORT=7813 ARXMCP_DATA_DIR=/some/path uv run python -m server.main 2>&1 | tail -30
observed: Every config-validation failure (unknown var, bad port, 0.0.0.0, data_dir with '..') prints a multi-frame Python traceback to stdout/stderr. The 0.0.0.0 ValidationError echoes the whole input dict: input_value={'bind_host': '0.0.0.0', ... 'data_dir': '.../scratchpad/api/data'}, disclosing the resolved data dir path in the error.
expected: Config errors are actionable in content (good messages incl. suggestions), but a shipped desktop app should surface a clean one-line FATAL, not a raw traceback, and should not echo the full config dict (with filesystem paths) into the error string. Low; startup-time stderr only.
code_ref: server/main.py:449 (_scan raise ValueError); server/config.py bind_host validator

title: 3-calls-per-session limit is STALE: real caps are 30 (search_papers) / 100 (get_chunk); boundary exact, error shape clean
observed: One session: search_papers calls 1-30 return normally, call 31 returns a clean MCP result envelope isError=true with body {"code":"RETRIEVAL_CAP_REACHED","limit":30,"message":"search_papers cap o..."}. No off-by-one (exactly 30 allowed), no HTTP error, no stack trace. get_chunk cap is 100. Cap is NOT documented in any tool description the agent/user sees.
expected: Confirms cost-control caps behave as coded (server/config.py max_search_papers_calls=30, max_get_chunk_calls=100). The task brief's '3-calls-per-session' constraint is out of date. Recording actual boundary + clean error shape.

title: Session retrieval cap trivially bypassed by new-session-per-call (counter resets to zero)
observed: Issuing initialize+initialized for a fresh Mcp-Session-Id before each search_papers call gives unlimited calls (each fresh session starts at count 0). 5/5 fresh-session calls succeeded past a session that had already hit its cap.
expected: Admitted, documented non-security behavior: server/session.py states these caps are 'cost control, NOT a security boundary' and lists 'rotating to a fresh server-issued id resets both counters at no cost' as a known, unpatched bypass inherent to per-session accounting without client identity. Recorded for completeness.

title: Bootstrap mode masks handler-level input validation — traversal/injection/NUL in paper_id/chunk_id all short-circuit to the stub envelope
observed: In ARXMCP_BOOTSTRAP_MODE=1, get_chunk(chunk_id='../../../../etc/passwd'), get_paper(paper_id="'; DROP TABLE"), search filters paper_id traversal, NUL bytes, RTL/emoji all return the 'No corpus ingested yet' stub (isError=false) because tools short-circuit BEFORE the handler validates the id. Schema-layer validation only enforces type/length/enum/range; the arXiv paper_id-format validation advertised in the tool descriptions is handler-level, so hostile ids pass the JSON-schema gate.
expected: Not a defect in isolation, but a real corpus is required to test handler-level traversal/injection defenses; bootstrap mode is not sufficient coverage for those attack classes. Follow-up: re-run get_chunk/get_paper/get_definitions traversal + NUL against a live corpus (ARXMCP_LANCEDB_PATH read-only).

title: Duplicate initialize on an already-initialized MCP session returns 200 (re-init allowed)
observed: After initialize + notifications/initialized on a session, a second initialize on the same Mcp-Session-Id returns 200 with a fresh initialize result. No error/idempotency guard.
expected: MCP spec does not strictly forbid re-init; recording as behavior. No observed state corruption. Info.

title: no-repro: HTTP-layer abuse
repro: scratchpad/api/http-abuse battery (chunked>1MB, Content-Length mismatch, dup Host, CRLF, malformed body)
observed: Chunked body >1 MB -> clean 413 payload_too_large; Content-Length mismatch (declare 1000, send 7, close) -> no crash, connection closed; duplicate Host headers -> 200 (first wins); CRLF in query param -> URL-encoded, not injected (200); malformed JSON -> clean -32700 parse error. No 500s, no hangs.
expected: HTTP boundary is robust for the tested abuse vectors.

title: no-repro: Concurrency / load / lifecycle
repro: 200 concurrent GET /healthz; 100 concurrent full MCP handshake+search; 80-socket slowloris; two servers same port; SIGTERM under load
observed: 200 concurrent /healthz -> all 200 (wall 0.69s); 100 concurrent MCP flows -> all 200 (wall 2.11s); 80 partial-header slowloris sockets did NOT block a normal request (served in 0.06s); second server on 7803 -> clean 'address already in use' then graceful shutdown, original unaffected; SIGTERM under a request loop -> graceful drain in ~2s, port freed, no orphan process.
expected: Async model handles concurrency, slowloris, port collision, and graceful shutdown correctly. No orphaned process on quit.

title: no-repro: Degraded-state / health honesty
repro: boot with ARXMCP_BOOTSTRAP_MODE=1 (no corpus); boot with ARXMCP_LANCEDB_PATH=<missing dir> and =<a file> without bootstrap
observed: Bootstrap: /readyz -> {"status":"bootstrap","bootstrap_mode_active":true,"warm":{...false}}; /status -> status 'warn'; /healthz -> 200 (liveness). Missing LanceDB path (no bootstrap) -> clean CorpusNotIngestedError startup refusal with actionable message; LanceDB path = a file -> same clean refusal. Health never reports 'healthy' when it is not.
expected: Degraded state is reported honestly; server refuses to start on cold-start corpus rather than lying.

title: no-repro: Config hostility
repro: boots with ARXMCP_FLUX_CAPACITOR=1; ARXMCP_BIND_PORT in {abc,0,70000}; ARXMCP_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0; ARXMCP_DATA_DIR=/tmp/../etc/foo
observed: Unknown var -> FATAL with difflib nearest-match suggestions; port 'abc' -> int_parsing ValidationError; port 0 and 70000 -> 'must be in [1024,65535]'; 0.0.0.0 -> rejected with loopback message (notes ARXMCP_UNSAFE_NETWORK_BIND=1 override); data_dir with '..' -> 'ARXMCP_DATA_DIR must not contain ..'. extra=forbid confirmed.
expected: All config hostility is caught at parse time with actionable messages (see CHAOS-API-08 for the traceback-noise nit).

title: no-repro: Information disclosure via schema / OpenAPI
observed: /openapi.json, /docs, /redoc all -> 404 {'detail':'Not Found'} (docs_url disabled). No token, env var, model path, or Python traceback found in any 4xx body from the running server. 4xx bodies are terse JSON ({'detail':...}).
expected: No schema/interactive-docs surface; runtime error bodies do not leak secrets. (Startup-time traceback leak recorded separately as CHAOS-API-08.)

title: no-repro: Auth timing + CSRF/DNS-rebind defenses
repro: grep hmac.compare_digest server/desktop_contract.py ; curl with evil Origin/Host/Sec-Fetch-Site
observed: Startup token comparison uses hmac.compare_digest (constant time) in server/desktop_contract.py:85 and server/desktop_child.py. Evil Origin -> 403 origin_forbidden; spoofed Host -> 421 Misdirected Request; Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site on /mcp -> 403 sec_fetch_site_forbidden (only /ui carved out, and /ui still enforces Origin+Host). No timing side-channel; CSRF/DNS-rebind well defended.
expected: Token compare is constant-time and the browser-facing attack surface (Origin/Host/Sec-Fetch-Site) is layered correctly.
